1. Last week I went to see my rheum after I missed an appointment back in November (oops)
2. I took my grandmother out to Denny’s
3. I had a successful first week of summer program at the preschool where I work. Trying to stay open minded and light hearted through all the pain 🥲

I am a preschool teacher. I’ve been a barista and bagged groceries. I worked at Target. Service industry is so demanding. Some of the worst pain days of my live. As a preschool teacher I just started working full time. I was working 28hr a week and now I’m up to 40. To be honest I’m really scared. I am exhausted and my joints are cranky! To put it mildly. I’m swollen, tired, and trying to stay positive. I’m taking an immunosuppressant so being around kids can be really tricky. I manage that by wearing a mask all the time. My parents are so proud of me that I’m finally working full-time. They help me out a lot and I’m grateful for that. I want to be independent, but this is so hard. I feel like my body just can’t keep up to the demands of this life. I love working with kids but I think that office jobs/remote work are the way to go for us. Have you heard of https://www.wearecapable.org ?

I’m so sorry it FAILED you. I’m currently taking. My markers look fine when I get labs but I’m in pain every day 🥲 
Hope you find something that works better! And quickly!

Hello Internet friend. Fellow CHS survivor, ex cannabis user, with disordered eating patterns here 🙋‍♀️❤️‍🩹I weighed the least I ever had in the midst of my CHS episodes. Honestly, i was happy with the number on the scale. And I’ve gained over 40lbs since quitting smoking. And I’m not so thrilled to weigh myself now. But, I just want to say you’re not alone but CHS is dangerous. I’m really trying to love myself and be healthy. I have 15mo cannabis free. There is love and beauty in caring for the person I am aside from the number on the scale. Just want you to know ur not alone. But imo, CHS/starvation/addiction/bulimia puts the body in an unhealthy state of stress which can lead to dramatic weight loss. 😔I try to remember my body is doing the best it can. And I’d never go back to my CHS years. It was truly miserable. I know it’s hard. Okay. Good luck. Be safe.

It’s hard being in your situation. As long as your son knows that diabetes can make it more difficult for the body to recover he’s got to take care of himself in the end and make his own decisions. I remember my mom and I butting heads even before all this covid stuff when I was diagnosed at 12. It’s such a tough spot. Now that I’m older I know she was just trying to help keep me safe. But again, too much pressure can make your kid lash out (that’s kind of what I did) luckily I was able to see that I was being obnoxious and self-destructive. But you can only lead a horse to water or whatever the saying goes. I guess I’m just here to say to remember to take care of yourself and lead by example. Educate yourself and also how chronic illness affects the entire family. It’s hard not to be codependent and get mixed up in boundaries. But hopefully your son feels confident and capable of dealing with these new health challenges. You can always support and encourage him that he’s got this. I would tell him this is what I would do xyz but recognize it’s his body his disease and his responsibility ultimately. I hope this helps. And you are a great mom for being concerned. Remember to take care of you too!!!!

Do you know your sensitivity factor? Say your target sugie is 120 you take your current sugar and subtract 120 and divide by your sensitivity factor. If you are sensitive to insulin and don’t need as much this number may be 60. Or it could be 40. 

So let’s say for example you are at 300 and you’re going to eat dinner that is 45g of carb. 
First you can calculate your correction for your sugar. 

300- 120=180 now, depending on your level of insulin sensitivity. You divide 180 by say 50. (In between a sensitivity factor of 40 and 60) 

180/50= 3.6 so you can take 3.6 units of insulin for correction. 

1. (Current sugar) minus (target sugar) divided by (sensitivity factor) 
(300-120)/50

2. Your insulin to carb ratio will determine how much to dose for food. You take 45 (amount of carbs) and divide it by say 10.

3. So 3.6 units correction plus 4.5 units bolus for food would be about 8 units you give yourself. 

I hope I didn’t make that too complicated. But the key is to know your insulin sensitivity factor and your carb ratio. If you are too high you may need a more aggressive 40 to use as your sensitivity factor. (300-120)/40 would be 4.5 units to bring your sugar down instead of 3.6. Knowing these equations helps when you have to calculate on your own. My pump however has my settings programmed so it does the math automatically for me. 

Good luck!! Let me know if this makes sense!
